decisions.statement: A refusal names the reading owed rather than only saying something is owed.
A refusal carries why the reading is owed.
A refusal names the page the warrant ran over, so why it is owed has a subject.
A warrant that ran over the page it names says nothing more than the rule.
A refusal names the read that would answer the warrant ready to run.
One read call names every page a refusal names.
A page a refusal names more than once is named once in that read.
A refusal for a body that moved says what the record holds and what is there now.
A refusal for a body read in part says how far that body reached the agent.
A list held back says how many readings are owed past the list and to call again.
A warrant owed of a taboo term is told from the rest by the page type its path names.
The refusal said of a taboo term asks the writer for a decision about the change.
The refusal said of a taboo term hands that term's whole page back.
A refusal handing a term's page back names running that same call again as the way through.
Which saying one owing takes is decided here rather than by the caller.
A refusal says nothing about how a read behaves.
Nothing here reads a file, reads the index, or asks which warrants there are.

definition: what a refusal says of one reading owed, composed from the warrant that owed it
